title: Appeal of Te Sang Soo Ryoo vs. Korean Capital Presbytery
disposition_detail: Appeal sustained: the SJC held that the Judicial Commission did not follow BCO 32 procedures because no indictment with witness list was served and the record lacked lower-court minutes or a hearing for the default judgment. The case was remanded to Presbytery for a new trial in compliance with BCO 32. The SJC expressly declined to rule on the adequacy of the two citations, on whether a default judgment without hearing and testimony is proper, or on the merits.
first_summary: The SJC sustained TE Te Sang Soo Ryoo's appeal from Korean Capital Presbytery, which had upheld a commission's suspension of him for heresy and schism. The SJC found the commission did not follow BCO 32 procedure because no indictment was served, and remanded for a new trial. It did not reach the merits.
summary: Korean Capital Presbytery's commission tried and suspended a Korean church assistant pastor for heresy and schism after he failed to answer two summonses, and Presbytery upheld the suspension. On appeal, the SJC sustained the procedural challenge because no indictment with witnesses had been served and the record lacked any minutes or hearing for the default judgment, contrary to BCO 32-3. The SJC remanded for a new trial but expressly declined to rule on the citations, default procedure, or merits.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2001-2, Appeal of Te Sang Soo Ryoo vs. Korean Capital Presbytery, Standing Judicial Commission, 30th General Assembly; adopted with 19 concur, 1 recused, 4 absent (lines 14, 84, 86-88).
evidence_notes.dispute: TE Ryoo was suspended for two years after a Korean Capital Presbytery commission judged him guilty of heresy and schism when he did not respond to summonses; Presbytery approved the commission's action and upheld the suspension, and he appealed (lines 31-41).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The SJC answered No to the procedural issue: the commission failed BCO 32 because no indictment with a witness list was served and the Record of the Case contained no minutes or hearing for the default judgment; remand for a new trial under BCO 32 (lines 47-51, 55-78).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The SJC expressly did not pass on the adequacy of the two citations, whether a default judgment without hearing and testimony is proper, or the merits (lines 80-82).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: None. The commission's judgment and Presbytery's approval are lower-court background actions, not incorporated decisions (lines 37-39, 41).

source_limits: Source is the published SJC report at pp. 122-124. The underlying lower-court Record of the Case and minutes are described but not supplied, so the synopsis does not assert whether the suspension itself was finally reversed or the merits resolved.
